Standard: Failure detection and fault isolation schemes are established and verified to support the failure response and PLOC requirements. All VCF failure modes are identified and the corresponding detection scheme provides 100% coverage for all safety-critical failures. Threshold and persistence values are set to ensure failures do not result in exceeding air vehicle transient limits for single failures or failure combinations when inserted during credible, worst-case flight conditions. Detected failures are isolated to the failed signal or component to support failure accommodation. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Review the VCF redundancy management design documentation to verify failure detection schemes are in place for all safety-critical signals and functions.
(2) Review failure detection schemes to verify the combination of in-line, cross-channel, or dissimilar sourced failure detection provides failure coverage. For designs that utilize a “last good value”, ensure that the design has a credible last value in all scenarios (e.g., when a dynamic signal is failed on power-up). Analysis.
  (1) Air vehicle transient analysis utilizing finalized threshold and persistence values demonstrates transients are within air vehicle established limits for all safety-critical single failures and combinations for all air vehicle configurations across the envelope, including during the catapult shot, takeoff rotation, and landing gear contact (bolter and touch and go).
  (2) Conduct failure detection analysis, including BIT coverage, to demonstrate 100% coverage for all safety-critical failures. Verify failures, which cannot be detected by BIT and are not easily inspected prior to flight, do not result in instability, LCO, or worse than Operational State II.
  (3) Verify failed signals and functions are isolated to prevent degraded VCF performance upon the detection of the failure. Test.
    (1) Lab test: Vehicle control function requirements-based testing (e.g., FQT) verifies failure detection and fault isolation schemes are properly implemented to meet system requirements.
    (2) Lab test: Failure modes and effects testing demonstrates a safe reaction to (within air vehicle transient limits), and recovery from, all safety-critical single failures and combinations identified from the air vehicle transient analysis. Ensure failures are inserted throughout the envelope, including during the catapult shot, takeoff rotation, and landing gear contact (bolter and touch and go).
